# Routing Patterns and Strategies

Dimension covering how teams make routing decisions in multi-model LLM
architectures. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

## Pattern Overview

| Pattern | Mechanism | Typical Savings | Quality Impact |
|---------|-----------|----------------|----------------|
| Task-based | Classifier routes by task type | 30-50% | Minimal if models matched well |
| Cost-based | Route to cheapest capable model | 35-85% [29] | 95% of frontier at best [29] |
| Latency-based | Route to fastest responding model | N/A | Faster TTFT |
| Quality-based (cascading) | Start small, escalate if needed | Up to 5× [34] | Maintained via verification |
| Fallback chains | Sequential provider attempts on failure | N/A (reliability) | Varies by fallback model |
| Semantic routing | Vector similarity for path selection | 40-70% [48] | N/A (routing, not inference) |
| A/B testing | Traffic splitting for evaluation | N/A (measurement) | N/A (measurement) |

## Task-Based Routing

Routes requests to different models based on task type (coding, summarization,
creative writing, etc.). The router examines query structure, complexity, and
domain [30].

**Implementation:** LangChain provides LLMRouterChain for directing inputs to
appropriate LLMs based on predefined criteria or dynamic conditions [30]. AWS
Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing automatically routes within model families
using prompt matching [39].

**Market context:** 37% of enterprises use 5+ models in production
environments (2026) [30].

## Cost-Based Routing

Dynamically selects between stronger (expensive) and weaker (cheap) models based
on predicted query difficulty [29].

**RouteLLM (LMSYS, ICLR 2025)** is the most rigorously benchmarked framework [29]:
- 85% cost reduction on MT Bench at 95% GPT-4 performance
- 45% reduction on MMLU
- 35% reduction on GSM8K
- Matrix factorization router: 95% GPT-4 performance using only 26% GPT-4 calls
  (48% cheaper than random routing)
- With data augmentation: 14% GPT-4 calls required (75% savings)
- Outperformed commercial offerings (Martian, Unify AI) by 40% lower cost

**Real-world case study [33]:** Customer support platform reduced monthly LLM
spend from $42,000 to $18,000 by routing simple queries to Claude 3.5 Haiku
and complex escalations to Claude 3.5 Sonnet — same CSAT scores.

**IBM estimate [70]:** Up to 85% reduction in inference expenses through
cascading routing.

## Latency-Based Routing

Chooses the model with fastest response time for real-time requirements [30].
Smaller models run faster, so lightweight queries get quicker responses.

**LiteLLM implementation [14]:** Tracks response times per deployment, selects
lowest-latency option. Configurable TTL windows and buffer thresholds prevent
overloading top performers. However, the "simple-shuffle" strategy is
recommended for production as latency-based adds significant overhead from
Redis operations [14].

**Semantic router [31]:** Reduces processing latency from 5000ms to 100ms using
lightweight vector math instead of LLM-based routing decisions.

## Quality-Based Routing (Cascading)

Starts with the smallest, cheapest model and escalates to more capable models
based on quality checks or confidence thresholds [70][34].

**Mechanisms for escalation [33]:**
- Self-consistency checks: generate multiple responses from cheap model; if they
  disagree significantly, escalate
- Confidence scoring: low confidence triggers escalation to larger model

**Measured results:**
- Cascading with reliable judges achieves 5× cost savings at zero or negligible
  performance degradation [34]
- Hybrid LLM approach: 40% fewer calls to large model with no quality drop [35]
- Confidence-aware routing: hallucination detection 0.74 vs 0.42 baseline,
  40% computational cost reduction [36]

## Fallback Chains

Sequential provider attempts when primary fails [45]. Each provider in the chain
is attempted until one succeeds or all options exhaust.

**Trigger conditions [45]:**
- 429 Too Many Requests → reroute to secondary provider
- 500, 502, 503, 529 → retry then fallback
- Do NOT count 400 (Bad Request) or 401 (Unauthorized)

**LiteLLM fallback types [15]:**
1. Standard fallbacks: triggered by all error types after retry exhaustion
2. Content policy fallbacks: specifically for ContentPolicyViolationError
3. Context window fallbacks: triggered by ContextWindowExceededError

**Streaming constraint [41]:** "Once we start sending tokens to a user, we
can't easily retry with a different model." Fallback only attempted if streaming
hasn't begun — most outages occur before first token [41].

## Semantic Routing

Uses vector embeddings to route requests based on semantic similarity rather
than waiting for LLM generation [31].

**vLLM Semantic Router v0.1 (Iris) [32]:** Six signal types — Domain
(MMLU-trained classification), Keyword (regex), Embedding (semantic
similarity), Factual (fact-check), Feedback (user satisfaction), Preference
(personalization). 600+ PRs merged, 300+ issues addressed, 50+ engineers [32].

**Aurelio Labs Semantic Router [31]:** MIT licensed, integrates with Cohere,
OpenAI, Hugging Face encoders. Works with in-memory or external vector
databases (Pinecone, Qdrant).

**Performance [48]:** Semantic caching combined with routing delivers 40-70%
cost reduction and improves latency from ~850ms to 120ms (7× speedup).

## A/B Testing and Experimentation

Traffic splitting between model variants for evaluation [37].

**Approaches [37][38]:**
- Weighted traffic distribution (50/50 or 90/10 splits)
- Canary releases: 1-5% traffic to new variant, monitor guardrails before
  increasing
- Shadow testing: both Control and Treatment receive requests, users only
  see Control responses

**Statistical requirements [38]:** At least 1,000 requests per variant for
statistical significance.

**Tools:** Istio VirtualService for Kubernetes-native splitting [37], feature
flagging systems for dynamic allocation, Thompson sampling for automatic
optimization [37].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Most routing benchmarks use MT Bench, MMLU, GSM8K — domain-specific performance
  (medical, legal) may differ significantly
- Multi-turn conversation routing is under-researched; most studies focus on
  single-query routing
- Router overhead vs savings trade-off: more sophisticated routers add latency
  and computational cost
- Model deprecation/version updates require router recalibration
- Adversarial gaming of routers (crafting prompts to force expensive model
  selection) is unexplored
